feature: Hour-long timeline: a zoom paints only what is on screen, and a scroll stops repainting
summary: Zooming the timeline of the 60 minute reference edit now paints only the window, not two and a half windows of clips, and clips sliding in with a scroll no longer start a fade that repainted the whole lane every frame. Zoom in 16-18 to about 12 ms a frame, scroll 15-16 to about 12 (p95 25 to 16).
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. File > Open the 60 minute reference edit (the speed walk's), or any long edit with hundreds of clips.

try.do: Open the hour-long edit and pinch the timeline in from Fit to about 8x, then back out.
Without zooming, scroll the timeline along quickly with two fingers.
Zoom in until clips show their pictures, then keep zooming: the pictures on a clip already on screen fade in.
Zoom out from far in: clips coming in at the edges arrive with their pictures, no fade.
Click a clip and a cut on the busy V1 track right after zooming, with the pointer held still.

evaluate: Does a pinch zoom on the hour-long edit feel smoother than yesterday, especially near Fit?
Does a fast scroll still show every clip's pictures and names where they should be, with nothing blank sliding in?
Do pictures coming in at the edges during a zoom out look right arriving at once rather than fading?
rough: Bars not reached yet: zoom median about 12-13 ms (near Fit 25-28 ms) and scroll about 12 ms against 8.3 ms; the task stays open.

Numbers, 60 min edit, markers down, same machine. Before (HEAD e873d3762, two runs): zoom in 16.1-18.1 ms median (p95 33.6-34.2), zoom out 14.8-16.3 (p95 33), scroll 14.3-16.4 (p95 23-29, 238-328 of 360 late). Zoom painting only the window: zoom in 11.4-11.8 (1x 25 ms, 128x+ 8), zoom out 14.4-15.0, scroll 15.2-15.8. Plus the strip fade fix: zoom in 13.4-13.5, zoom out 12.9-13.3 (p95 25), scroll 11.7-12.3 (p95 16.2-16.7, 137-159 late). Load average on the Mac was 9-11 during the last runs, from other work, so the far-zoom octaves read 2-3 ms higher than the run before.
Edits (trim, move, blade, undo) unchanged at 38-99 ms against 16; mostly the inspector, owned by a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed.

The same window photographed after a scroll (wide painting) and after a zoom (window only) differs only where pictures were still being read in the first shot and by a pixel on three transition band outlines (a throwaway walk: 60 min edit, three zooms in, one pan along, a zoom in and out back to the same window).

Tried first and backed out: painting each lane in fixed half-window pieces of time, each its own canvas. Every canvas is a GPU texture of its own and a zoom resized each one every frame: scroll and zoom both went to 25 ms. Written into docs/design/video.md 8f so nobody tries it again.
